title: 157. Design HashMap

examples.explanation: put(1,1), put(2,2); get(1) is 1, get(3) is -1. After put(2,1) updates key 2, get(2) is 1; after remove(2), get(2) is -1.
Initially get(5) is -1. After put(5,7), get(5) is 7; after remove(5), get(5) is -1.
No get calls, so every entry is null.

hints: Store the entries in a hash map: put inserts or updates, remove deletes, get looks up with a -1 default.
A direct array of size 1000001 with a -1 sentinel also works since keys are bounded.
Construction, put and remove report "null"; each get reports the plain integer result.
